title: Deep Past Challenge - Translate Akkadian to English (archived competition page excerpt)
why_relevant: Contains the authoritative statement of the evaluation metric (geometric mean of BLEU and chrF++) and rules excerpt about external data/models and internet-off requirement for Kaggle notebooks.
extracted_technique: Implement corpus BLEU + chrF++ and optimize gmean; enforce offline-only behavior on Kaggle while allowing local caching.
query: deep-past-initiative-machine-translation external data allowed internet disabled evaluation metric geometric mean BLEU chrF++
takeaway: Use corpus-level BLEU and chrF++ and combine via geometric mean. External public data/models are allowed, but Kaggle notebooks should run with internet disabled, so weights must be packaged or pre-downloaded.

title: ByT5: Towards a token-free future with pre-trained byte-to-byte models
why_relevant: Justifies selecting byte-level T5 variants for noisy transliteration and uncommon characters; informs training/decoding choices and expected robustness vs subword tokenization.
extracted_technique: Fine-tune a byte-level encoder-decoder (ByT5) for translation; byte inputs avoid tokenizer OOV issues.
takeaway: Byte-level seq2seq models are well-suited to domains with unusual symbols/orthography. Fine-tuning ByT5 is a strong default for transliteration-to-English translation tasks.

title: chrF++: words helping character n-grams
why_relevant: chrF++ is half of the competition metric; understanding its character n-gram nature motivates character-preserving normalization and decoding strategies (and MBR scoring based on chrF).
extracted_technique: Use chrF++ (character n-gram F-score with word boundary info) as a primary metric and as an MBR utility function proxy.
takeaway: chrF++ is robust to tokenization noise and rewards character-level overlap, which fits transliteration-heavy MT. Optimize decoding/postprocessing to preserve characters and consistent formatting.

title: Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding for Neural Machine Translation
why_relevant: Supports using MBR decoding (reranking a candidate pool) to improve translation quality under overlap-based metrics when references are unavailable at test time.
extracted_technique: Generate a pool (beam + sampled candidates) and choose the hypothesis minimizing expected loss under a similarity metric (e.g., chrF) over the pool.
query: minimum bayes risk decoding neural machine translation Müller Sennrich 2021
takeaway: MBR can improve generation stability by selecting candidates that are most central under a metric like chrF, aligning well with BLEU/chrF-style evaluation. It is practical for Kaggle inference with modest candidate counts.
